info.name: WinX88 — Marketing Channels & Meta CAPI
info.description:
End-to-end flow for third-party media buyers: campaign tracking links, vendor reporting API, and Meta Conversions API.

RUN THE FOLDERS IN ORDER. Folder 1 is one-time setup per agency; folders 2-4 simulate what ad traffic, your frontend and your admins do; folder 5 is what the agency sees.

## Before you start

Set these collection variables (Variables tab):
- `baseUrl` — the API host. PRODUCTION IS `https://safurion.online`, NOT winx-88.com. winx-88.com serves the website and has no API routes.
- `adminToken` — from Admin Login
- `userToken` — from a player login/register

The rest (`vendorId`, `channelCode`, `cid`, `vendorApiKey`) are filled in as you run the steps.

## The three link forms

1. `https://safurion.online/c/<code>` — always works.
2. `https://winx-88.com/c/<code>` — only works once a Cloudflare Redirect Rule forwards `/c/*` to the API. Better for Facebook ad review since it is your brand domain.
3. `https://winx88.net/?channel=<code>` — needs the frontend beacon; loses clicks when JS is blocked.

## What is NOT deployed yet

At time of writing, everything in folders 4-5 involving Meta CAPI is on the dev branch only, and the frontend does not yet forward `channel`/`cid` at registration — so registrations will not attribute until that ships.

item.name: 1. Setup — run once per agency (admin)
item.description:
Steps 1.1 to 1.3 are the ONLY setup you perform. After 1.3 you have everything to hand the agency: the tracking links and their API key.

Requires the `marketing.manage` RBAC permission (or SUPER_ADMIN, which bypasses all checks).

request.description:
Creates the agency.

**COPY THE RETURNED `id` INTO THE `vendorId` COLLECTION VARIABLE.** Steps 1.2 and 1.3 both need it, and 1.3 takes it in the URL path where a stale value silently issues a key to the wrong agency.

One channel per CAMPAIGN, not per agency. This is what produces the tracking link.

- `vendorId` goes in the BODY here (contrast with 1.3, where it is in the URL).
- `code` is what appears in the link. Lowercased automatically; letters, digits, `_`, `-` only.
- `landingPath` — set to `/register`. If you leave it at some test value, visitors land on the wrong page.
- `pixelId` — OPTIONAL. The agency's own Meta pixel. When set, the link carries `&pixel=` and server-side conversions report to it. Your own site pixel keeps firing regardless — never replaced.
- `capiAccessToken` — optional per-agency Meta token, when their pixel lives in their own Business Manager.

**Ignore `trackingUrl` in the response if it shows winx-88.com** — that comes from `APP_BASE_URL` on the server. The working link is `{{baseUrl}}/c/<code>`.

**The vendor id is in the URL PATH, not the body.** The body only carries an optional label. That is what binds the key to the agency.

**The plaintext `apiKey` is shown ONCE.** Only its SHA-256 hash is stored; it cannot be recovered. Copy it into `vendorApiKey` now.

Check `vendor_name` in the response matches the agency you intended before sending the key to anyone — with a stale `vendorId` you would hand one agency another's key and never know.

Rotation: issue a new key, let them switch, then DELETE the old one. Both work during the overlap.

Replace the trailing `1` with the key id from 1.3.

item.name: 2. Tracking — what ad traffic does (public)
item.description: You do NOT run these in normal operation. 2.1 is hit by real ad clicks; 2.2 is called by your frontend. They are here so you can smoke-test the pipe before handing links to the agency.

query.description: Facebook appends this to the ad destination automatically. Captured server-side so a deposit approved days later can still be matched to the ad.

request.description:
**THIS IS THE LINK YOU GIVE THE AGENCY.** Every ad click hits it.

Turn OFF automatic redirect following (Settings → Automatically follow redirects) to see the 302 Location header.

The redirect preserves ALL incoming query params and appends ours:
`?fbclid=…&sub=…&channel=…&cid=…&pixel=…`

Preserving `fbclid` matters — dropping it silently breaks Facebook attribution and any later Conversions API match.

An unregistered code still redirects (never 404 a paid click) but is flagged `is_unknown` and appears in 4.2.

response.name: 302 — redirect carrying fbclid, cid and pixel
response.body:
Found. Redirecting to https://winx-88.com/register?fbclid=IwAR_REAL_CLICK_XYZ&sub=creative_7&channel=capi_test&cid=7ff17d71-8f68-41b3-8be0-582d439acce1&pixel=999888777666555

COPY THE cid VALUE INTO THE {{cid}} COLLECTION VARIABLE for step 3.1.

response.name: 302 — UNKNOWN code still redirects (never 404 a paid click)
response.body:
Found. Redirecting to https://winx-88.com/register?channel=typo_code&cid=d864acf9-1020-4c56-906a-d3fbda332b3e

The click is stored with is_unknown = true and shows in 4.2 Unknown Click Codes.
Registering the channel LATER does NOT retro-link these clicks — catch typos early.

request.description:
Called BY YOUR FRONTEND, never by you. Covers visitors who land on any page with `?channel=` without passing through `/c/:code` — e.g. traffic pointed straight at winx88.net.

Returns the click id so the signup can still be tied to a click, plus the campaign's bound pixel.

Rate limited to 120/min per IP. Call once per session, not per page view.

item.name: 3. Player journey — attribution & conversion
item.description: Simulates what a real player does after clicking the ad. This is where attribution is actually created, and where the Meta conversion events originate.

header.description: Which of your domains the signup came from. Captured into users.signup_domain and shown as Channel Name for Direct signups.

request.description:
`channel` and `cid` are the NEW optional fields. Everything else is unchanged, and the signup FORM does not change — no new fields for the user.

BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: omit both and registration behaves exactly as before, creating no attribution row.

Effects when `channel` is present:
- a `user_channel_attribution` row (FIRST TOUCH WINS — never overwritten)
- `source = REDIRECT` if the `cid` is valid for that channel, else `PARAM`
- a `CompleteRegistration` event queued to Meta, if the campaign has a pixel bound

A forged or mismatched `cid` is silently discarded — the registration still counts, just without a linked click.

response.name: 201 — registered and attributed

formdata.description: Which of the player's OWN numbers they paid from. Validated server-side against user_phone_numbers — another user's number is rejected. Format-tolerant. Omit to default to their primary.

request.description: Creates a PENDING deposit. No conversion is sent yet — Facebook only hears about it when an admin APPROVES it (step 3.3).

response.name: 400 — playerNumber belongs to someone else

request.description:
**THIS is the moment the Meta conversion is created.** Replace 357 with the deposit id.

Inside the SAME transaction that approves the deposit, the backend:
1. counts prior approved deposits — zero means this is the player's first (`is_ftd`)
2. resolves the player's campaign and its bound pixel
3. queues a `Purchase` event

Because the queue write shares the transaction, a conversion can never exist for a deposit that rolled back, nor be lost for one that committed. Meta is never called inline — that would hold the wallet row lock across an HTTP round trip.

No event is produced for: a REJECTED deposit, or a player with no campaign attribution (organic).

Both the manual admin path and the automated WinyPay PSP path go through this same method, so both produce conversions.

item.name: 4. Verify — admin monitoring
item.description: The screens to check during a campaign launch. 4.2 especially: check it DAILY in the first week.

query.description: PENDING | SENT | FAILED | SKIPPED. Omit for all.

request.description:
**The screen that answers "why has Facebook stopped receiving our conversions".**

`enabled: false` means META_CAPI_ENABLED is off — events queue but nothing is sent. That is the shipping default, deliberately: the outbox fills so you can inspect it before anything reaches Meta.

Status meanings:
- `PENDING` — queued, will be attempted by the once-a-minute sweeper
- `SENT` — Meta accepted it
- `FAILED` — gave up. Either a permanent rejection (bad token, no pixel access — a 4xx from Meta, not worth retrying) or 5 exhausted attempts

Transient failures back off 1m → 5m → 25m → 2h → 10h. `last_error` carries Meta's own message.

request.description:
**Check this DAILY during a campaign launch.**

Lists codes seen in real traffic that match no registered channel — i.e. a typo in a live ad, or a link nobody told you about. Those clicks are paid for and are NOT counted for any vendor.

Registering the channel afterwards does NOT retro-link them. Catching a typo on day one instead of day seven is the entire value of this endpoint.

response.name: 200 — a typo caught in the wild

item.name: 4.3 Member list — Channel Type / Channel Name

request.description:
Every member row carries `channel_type` and `channel_name`, showing where that player came from.

PRECEDENCE (by who gets paid): **Affiliate > Refer A Friend > Marketing > Direct**. A player matching two sources shows the one with the payout attached, so this list never contradicts the affiliate commission reports. The underlying rows are all preserved.

| channel_type | channel_name |
|---|---|
| Affiliate | the affiliate's username |
| Refer A Friend | the referrer's username |
| Marketing | the campaign name |
| Direct | which of your domains they signed up on |

`Direct` with a null name means they registered before signup_domain existed — not recoverable.

The same two fields appear on `/user/admin/search` and `/user/admin/members/search`.

item.name: 5. Vendor API — what the agency calls
item.description:
Authenticated by `x-api-key`, NOT a JWT. The agency never gets an admin token, a login, or database access.

Scoping is enforced in SQL: the vendor id comes from the key itself, so no parameter can widen it. Responses are aggregates only — never a username, user id, phone, email or IP.

request.description:
Lists ONLY the calling vendor's campaigns.

Key format is `<prefix>.<secret>` — send it verbatim, exactly as returned by 1.3. Do not prepend a domain, and do not strip the `mk_` prefix; both produce 401.

query.description: total | day. For day, both dates are required and the range caps at 92 days.
Optional. Restrict to one campaign code.

request.description:
The agency's report. Rate limited to 60/min per key.

### Counting rules — the ones that cause invoice arguments

**`ftds` counts a player's FIRST-EVER approved deposit, not their first in the window.** So `ftds` is normally LOWER than `depositCount`, and `ftdAmount` lower than `depositTotal`. In the saved response below: 3 deposits, only 2 FTDs. That is correct, not a bug.

**Registrations count on the REGISTRATION date, not the click date.** A click on the 1st that becomes a signup on the 5th appears in both days separately. There is no lookback window.

**Only APPROVED deposits count**, on their approval date.

**First touch wins** — a player who arrives via campaign A then B is credited to A permanently.

**Expect these numbers to run 10-30% BELOW the agency's ad platform.** Facebook counts modelled and view-through conversions; we count only what reached our servers. Agree this before launch.

`trackingSince` is their first recorded click — anything earlier legitimately returns zeros, because there is no historical backfill.

response.name: 400 — day range over 92 days
